# Agent CLI Reference

Canonical reference for the ClaudeClaw agent-facing CLIs. This block is generated from each CLI's exported `descriptor` — do not hand-edit it; run `npm run gen:cli-docs` to regenerate. The runtime injects the correct absolute `PROJECT_ROOT` into your prompt; use that value and invoke a CLI as `node "$PROJECT_ROOT/<binary>" <command>`. Do NOT rediscover the root with `git rev-parse` or search the filesystem — a non-repo cwd can anchor onto the wrong checkout (see issue #157).

## Index

- [`agent-create-cli`](#agent-create-cli) — Non-interactively create a ClaudeClaw agent (used by the Telegram agent or CI).
- [`hive-cli`](#hive-cli) — Store-aware hive-mind accessor — the ONLY sanctioned way to read/write hive_mind.
- [`meet-cli`](#meet-cli) — Send an agent into a video meeting as a real-time AI avatar (Pika or Daily.co).
- [`mission-cli`](#mission-cli) — Create and manage one-shot mission tasks executed by a target agent.
- [`schedule-cli`](#schedule-cli) — Manage RECURRING scheduled tasks (cron) that fire in an agent process.
- [`slack-cli`](#slack-cli) — Read and post to Slack from an agent (JSON output).

## agent-create-cli

Non-interactively create a ClaudeClaw agent (used by the Telegram agent or CI).

Binary: `node dist/agent-create-cli.js`

### Commands

- `agent-create-cli --id ID --name NAME --description DESC [--runtime-mode messenger|headless] [--lifecycle persistent|task-scoped] [--token TOKEN] [--model MODEL] [--template TEMPLATE] [--activate]` — Create an agent. Messenger mode requires --token; headless mode does not. Headless lifecycle defaults to persistent; task-scoped workers drain and deactivate after their work completes.
- `--validate --token TOKEN` — Only validate the Telegram bot token, then exit.
- `--suggest --id ID` — Print suggested bot names for the given --id as JSON, then exit.
- `--templates` — List available templates, then exit.

### Notes

- --id must be lowercase with no spaces; --name and --description are required for creation.
- --token is a Telegram bot token from @BotFather.
- Creating or activating a new headless worker identity requires explicit user authorization. Do not infer authorization from a request for delegation or parallelism.
- Task-scoped workers deactivate automatically after their work drains, but agent identity and history are never deleted automatically.

## hive-cli

Store-aware hive-mind accessor — the ONLY sanctioned way to read/write hive_mind.

Binary: `node dist/hive-cli.js`

### Commands

- `path` — Print the resolved hive-mind DB absolute path. Does NOT open the DB (works without DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY) — answers "where is my store?".
- `read [--limit N]` — Print the most recent hive_mind entries (default 10).
- `log --action <action> --summary <summary> [--agent <id>]` — Append a hive_mind entry. --agent defaults to CLAUDECLAW_AGENT_ID (or "main"). Log after any meaningful action so the fleet can see it.

### Notes

- Resolves the store via config.ts STORE_DIR (honors the .env CLAUDECLAW_STORE_DIR pin) — never re-derives from process.env.
- Never touch hive_mind with a raw sqlite3 call against a build-relative path; it can silently hit the wrong (e.g. live) DB when the store is relocated.

## meet-cli

Send an agent into a video meeting as a real-time AI avatar (Pika or Daily.co).

Binary: `node dist/meet-cli.js`

### Commands

- `join --meet-url <url> [--agent <id>] [--brief <file>] [--auto-brief] [--context <hint>] [--bot-name <name>] [--voice-id <id>] [--meeting-password <pw>]` — Pika avatar mode: the bot joins an existing Google Meet / Zoom URL with a real-time AI avatar. --agent defaults to main.
- `join-daily [--agent <id>] [--mode direct|auto] [--brief <file>] [--auto-brief] [--context <hint>] [--bot-name <name>] [--room-name <slug>] [--ttl-sec <seconds>]` — Daily.co mode: create a new Daily room, spawn a Pipecat agent in it, and return the room URL to share. Requires DAILY_API_KEY and GOOGLE_API_KEY.
- `brief --meet-url <url> [--agent <id>] [--context <hint>]` — Run the pre-flight research pipeline and write a system-prompt brief file to the temp dir using the agent's full stack.
- `leave --session-id <id>` — Make the bot leave a meeting / tear down the Daily room.
- `list [--active]` — List recent meet sessions, or only live ones with --active.
- `show --session-id <id>` — Show full detail for one meet session.

### Notes

- Output is JSON on stdout: {"ok": true, ...} on success or {"ok": false, "error": ...} on failure.
- Pika mode requires PIKA_DEV_KEY and resolves avatars from warroom/avatars/<agent>-meet.png (falling back to <agent>.png).

## mission-cli

Create and manage one-shot mission tasks executed by a target agent.

Binary: `node dist/mission-cli.js`

### Commands

- `create [--agent <id>] [--title "Label"] [--priority N] [--at <RFC3339>] "Full prompt text"` — Queue a one-shot mission task immediately, or gate it until a future RFC 3339 timestamp with --at. The timestamp must include Z or an explicit UTC offset. --agent assigns it (omit to leave unassigned for dashboard auto-assign); --title defaults to the first 60 chars of the prompt; --priority defaults to 5.
- `workflow --agent <worker> [--owner <coordinator>] --objective "Outcome" [--title "Label"] [--max-depth N] [--max-tasks N] [--max-fanout N] [--deadline <RFC3339>] [--at <RFC3339>] [--key <idempotency-key>] "Initial task prompt"` — Create an explicit durable mission workflow and its initial worker task. The scheduler persists each outcome, wakes the owner with full workflow context, and enforces immutable depth, task, fan-out, and deadline bounds.
- `handback <task-id> "Report text"` — Report back on the running task you were assigned. Routes deterministically to the task's originator (created_by) — another agent, or the human via the primary agent. Repeated calls return the one canonical handback instead of queueing duplicates.
- `continue <task-id> "Next-step prompt" --key <idempotency-key> [--max-steps N]` — Queue one next step from the currently running task in an explicitly bounded self-directed chain. The first step fixes the chain limit; every request requires a stable idempotency key, and repeated calls from the same parent return its canonical child.
- `cancel-chain <chain-id>` — Persistently stop a self-directed continuation chain and cancel its queued next steps. A running step may finish but cannot advance the cancelled chain.
- `transition <coordinator-task-id> <disposition> --key <idempotency-key> [--agent <id>] [--task "agent:prompt" ...] [--reason "Text"] "Next prompt"` — Apply exactly one validated transition to a durable workflow outcome. Dispositions: complete, dispatch, gather, continue_self, retry, wait_for_human, block, fail. Dispatch-like transitions are checked against workflow bounds before any task is queued.
- `governor-status` — Show read-only Crew Mission governor state, five-hour turn allowance, active reservations, parked work, and provider/model usage.
- `governor-enable --reason "Operator reason" [--for-minutes N]` — Enable Crew Missions for 1-1440 minutes. Main operator only. Every change is durably audited and automatically expires.
- `governor-disable --reason "Operator reason"` — Immediately disable Crew Missions. Main operator only. The change is durably audited.
- `workflow-list [--status <status>]` — List durable workflows with owner, status, objective, and persisted bounds.
- `workflow-result <workflow-id>` — Show one durable workflow with its tasks, outcomes, bounds, and terminal reason.
- `workflow-cancel <workflow-id>` — Durably cancel a workflow and its queued work. A running task may finish recording its outcome but cannot advance the workflow.
- `workflow-resume <workflow-id> "Human answer"` — Resume a workflow in waiting_human by recording the answer durably and queueing one coordinator wake-up.
- `gather --summary-agent <id> --title "Label" --task "agent:prompt" [--task "agent:prompt" ...] "join/summary prompt"` — Non-blocking fan-out: queue one child task per --task, then a parked join task for --summary-agent. The scheduler releases the join with all child results once the last child finishes, producing ONE consolidated summary. Children finish with their findings as output — they do NOT handback.
- `list [--status <status>]` — List mission tasks, optionally filtered by status (e.g. queued).
- `result <id>` — Show a task with its status and result (or error) once it has run.
- `cancel <id>` — Cancel a queued task (no-op if it already completed).

### Notes

- Immediate tasks are normally claimed within ~60s. Tasks created with --at stay queued until the UTC availability gate opens.
- Every mission runs once, reaches a terminal status, and auto-purges after 7 days through normal mission retention.
- The creating agent is recorded from CLAUDECLAW_AGENT_ID (defaults to "main").
- Orchestration modes: delegate (create, 1->1 async), await (orchestrator fires N creates and waits inline — no CLI verb), gather (1->N non-blocking join). Handbacks resolve to the originator.

## schedule-cli

Manage RECURRING scheduled tasks (cron) that fire in an agent process.

Binary: `node dist/schedule-cli.js`

### Commands

- `create "prompt text" "cron expression" [--agent <id>]` — Create a recurring task from a prompt and a cron expression. Rejects invalid cron. --agent defaults to CLAUDECLAW_AGENT_ID or "main".
- `list [--agent <id>]` — List scheduled tasks with next/last run times. "main" lists all agents; any other --agent scopes to that agent.
- `delete <id>` — Delete a scheduled task.
- `pause <id>` — Pause a scheduled task without deleting it.
- `resume <id>` — Resume a paused scheduled task.

### Notes

- For RECURRING jobs (cron). For one-shot tasks, use mission-cli instead.
- Cron examples: "0 9 * * 1" (Mon 9am), "0 8 * * *" (daily 8am), "0 */4 * * *" (every 4h).
- Tasks fire from the resolved agent's scheduler, not the main bot.

## slack-cli

Read and post to Slack from an agent (JSON output).

Binary: `node dist/slack-cli.js`

### Commands

- `list [--limit N]` — List Slack conversations (default limit 20). Prints JSON.
- `read <channel_id> [--limit N]` — Read recent messages from a channel (default limit 15). Prints JSON.
- `send <channel_id> "message" [--thread-ts TS]` — Send a message to a channel, optionally replying in a thread.
- `search <query>` — Find conversations whose name contains the query (case-insensitive). Prints JSON.
